data.content_ref: inline:The refutation condition ('if the zero-inclusion case yields a count other than 144') refutes only the *correctness of the arithmetic*, not the existence of the *shared mechanism*. Even if the zero-inclusion count were miscalculated, both artifacts could still split on zero-inclusion to handle the hundreds-digit asymmetry — the mechanism would be shared but misapplied. A valid refutation of 'shared mechanism' must show one artifact does NOT split on zero-inclusion (e.g., handles the asymmetry via a different method), not that a particular count from that split is wrong.
